title: Netting an FBN Inbound Shortage Across Shipment Lines
content:
When a Fulfilled by Northloop (FBN) shipment was sent under the minimal split placement option, the netted shortage is measured over the whole shipment: the units expected on all of its lines less the units received on all of them; when it was sent under any other placement option and the shipment carries at least two lines, the claimed one included, with the same declared unit cost, the netted shortage is measured over those same-cost lines together, so that units of a look-alike SKU received in excess offset the claimed line. A shipment meeting neither description is netted on the claimed line alone under this rule.

The placement option is the split option recorded with the shipment's inbound placement fee. The declared unit cost of a line is the one on its inbound receipt.

## Scope of netting

| Placement option of the shipment | Lines sharing the claimed line's declared unit cost (claimed line included) | Netted over |
|---|---|---|
| minimal split | any number | every line of the shipment |
| partial split or Northloop-optimized split | 2 or more | the same-cost lines together |
| partial split or Northloop-optimized split | 1 (the claimed line only) | the claimed line alone |

## Example (hypothetical shipment)

| Line | Declared unit cost | Expected | Received |
|---|---|---|---|
| SKU A (claimed) | 12.00 | 50 | 40 |
| SKU B | 12.00 | 30 | 36 |
| SKU C | 20.00 | 20 | 15 |

- Sent under partial split: lines A and B share 12.00, two lines in all, so the netted shortage is 80 expected less 76 received, which is 4.
- Sent under minimal split: all lines count, 100 expected less 91 received, which is 9.
- Sent under partial split with SKU B declared at 13.00 instead: only the claimed line has 12.00, and the netted shortage is 50 less 40, which is 10.
